primary_claim: Internal state controllability (Lindsey 2025's think/don't-think effect) replicates across 14 open-weight models spanning Qwen3, Gemma 3, and Tulu 3 families from 0.3B to 235B parameters with no clear trend in the think vs. don't-think gap across scale, and prompted attempts to evade a deception probe via explicit suppression instructions fail to reduce probe performance in Qwen3-32B and Qwen3-14B during sandbagging.

effect.metric: think vs don't-think cosine-similarity gap; deception-probe AUC under evasion instructions
effect.value: effect present across all 14 models with no clear size trend; probe scores remain within noise of (or above) baseline at every probed layer for Qwen3-32B/-14B under ignore/suppress/probed evasion instructions

contradicts_or_qualifies: Lindsey (2025) observes that earlier/less capable Claude models show a larger think-don't-think gap; this replication finds no clear trend with model size across Qwen and Gemma families

Testing the focus/ignore prompt framings from Gurnee et al. 2026 finds they give no more controllability than the original think/don't-think prompts, despite being shown to give more control over the J-Space in that work
stated_future_work: Mechanistic analysis of attention circuits to confirm the 'attention-tagging' theory of why controllability occurs
limitations_stated: With few models per family, cannot fully rule out a scale trend even though none is observed
With only a single family (Tulu) tested with DPO checkpoints, cannot say whether DPO's gap-reducing effect is general
Not completely clear whether Gemma or smaller Qwen models truly lack 'silent' representations or just show a smaller version of the late-layer drop
quote: the effect replicates in 14 open-weight models from 0.3B to 235B parameters (Qwen3, Gemma 3, Tulu 3) with no clear trend in the think vs. don't-think gap across scale
